findings.deck_quote: Uncertainty and cash = PRE1 + GAP + POST
findings.problem: PRE1, GAP, and POST are relied on in the empirical roadmap before the deck defines them. Their first plain-language definitions appear on slide 9.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json pages 4 and 9; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slides 4 and 9; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Methodology and Empirical Design, defines PRE1 as one quarter before announcement, GAP as announced but not closed, and POST as after completion.
findings.why_it_matters: RQ2 is the audience's first map of the timing design, so a first-time listener cannot decode the equation without silently guessing or waiting five slides.
findings.suggested_action: Replace the symbols with plain-language stages on slide 4, or define them at first use: PRE1 (one quarter before), GAP (announced, not closed), and POST (after completion).

findings.deck_quote: Thesis framework: Verrecchia (1983); Dye (1985); Basic (1988); Rule 10b-5; Matsumoto et al. (2011); Hollander et al. (2010)
findings.problem: The footer presents a court decision and an SEC rule in the same undifferentiated list as disclosure theory and empirical conference-call research. It also shortens the thesis author form Basic Inc. v. Levinson (1988) to Basic (1988), making the case look like an academic author citation.
findings.evidence: _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Conceptual Framework, identifies Basic as a Court holding and Rule 10b-5 as legal authority; the reference list gives Basic Inc. v. Levinson (1988) and the SEC Rule 10b-5 entry. The same section uses Verrecchia and Dye as theory and Matsumoto and Hollander as academic evidence.
findings.why_it_matters: The statement that a firm may stay silent but cannot mislead depends on legal authority, and the current source line obscures that evidentiary role.
findings.suggested_action: Separate the footer into disclosure theory, legal authorities, and earnings-call evidence, and print Basic Inc. v. Levinson (1988) in full.

findings.deck_quote: Calls with an estimated UncResCEO measure.
findings.problem: UncResCEO is used as a named measure before the deck introduces or decodes the symbol. The definition appears on slide 7.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json pages 6 and 7; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slides 6 and 7; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Estimation of the Main Variable, defines UncResCEO as the residual part of CEO answer uncertainty left after the first-stage decomposition.
findings.why_it_matters: The sample funnel asks the audience to understand what qualifies the 44,900 calls, but the measure name is opaque at that point.
findings.suggested_action: Write Calls with an estimated residual CEO uncertainty measure (UncResCEO) on slide 6, then retain the short label thereafter.

findings.deck_quote: one SD from zero; SE; Approx. 95% CI
findings.problem: The statistical abbreviations SD, SE, and CI are used without being expanded before reliance. The deck later continues with the same shorthand.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json pages 7 through 10 and thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slides 7 through 10. No audience-facing legend expands these abbreviations before their first use.
findings.why_it_matters: The quantities are compact but load-bearing, and a listener should not have to translate the labels while also following the substantive result.
findings.suggested_action: Add one compact first-use legend: SD = standard deviation; SE = standard error; CI = confidence interval.

findings.deck_quote: Leverage, size, Tobin's Q, ROA, capex, dividends, cash-flow volatility
findings.problem: The same control set is named differently on later slides: slide 8 says size and dividends, while slides 9 and 10 say ln(assets) and dividend indicator. The latter wording identifies the actual variables; the former can imply a different size measure and a continuous dividend amount.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json pages 8 through 10; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Methodology and Empirical Design and Appendix II, defines lnAssets as the natural log of assets and DivDummy as a dividend-payer indicator.
findings.why_it_matters: An examiner comparing specifications may reasonably wonder whether the controls changed across findings.
findings.suggested_action: Use the same labels on all three slides, preferably ln(assets) and dividend indicator, or introduce them once as firm size measured by ln(assets) and dividend-payer indicator.

findings.problem: ns is used repeatedly as a result label but is never defined as not statistically significant.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json pages 9 and 10; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slides 9 and 10. The deck supplies no legend for ns.
findings.why_it_matters: Unlike the displayed p-value thresholds, ns has no spoken or written decoding on the deck.
findings.suggested_action: Add ns = not statistically significant to the first statistical legend, or replace each ns with not significant.

findings.deck_quote: POST dip is marginal; not over-read
findings.problem: The second clause is missing the verb and object needed for speech. It cannot be read aloud as written without changing it to an instruction or passive construction.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json page 9; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slide 9; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Main Analysis 2, says the POST uncertainty estimate should not be over-read.
findings.why_it_matters: This annotation carries an interpretive boundary, and a grammatical stumble weakens the caution at the moment it is needed.
findings.suggested_action: Use The POST dip is marginal; do not over-read it.

findings.deck_quote: Cash adds its own lag: 0.7547 (SE 0.0108), p < .01.
findings.problem: Cash does not add a lag. The cash-ratio regression includes the outcome's own lag, so the written subject makes the sentence semantically and orally awkward.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json page 9; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slide 9; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Methodology and Empirical Design, states that the CashRatio outcome adds its own one-quarter within-firm lag.
findings.why_it_matters: The current wording makes the model specification sound like an action performed by the cash variable.
findings.suggested_action: Use The cash-ratio regression includes its own one-quarter lag: 0.7547 (SE 0.0108), p < .01.

findings.deck_quote: Documents that the language pattern concentrates in cash acquisitions rather than stock.
findings.problem: The comparison is grammatically unbalanced: cash acquisitions is compared with stock, rather than with stock acquisitions.
findings.evidence: deck_text_extracted(4).json page 11; thesis_defense_main_deck_slides_01-13_standardized_v2(5).pdf slide 11; _thesis_FLAT(3).tex, Introduction contribution paragraph and Conclusion, consistently compare cash acquisitions with stock acquisitions.
findings.why_it_matters: The intended contrast is clear, but a presenter must silently repair the final phrase to say it naturally.
findings.suggested_action: Use Documents that the language pattern concentrates in cash acquisitions rather than in stock acquisitions.

clean_dimensions: Citation support: no cited work is attached to a proposition outside the role for which the thesis uses it.
Citation existence and years: no new exception beyond the operator-settled status.
Author identity: otherwise consistent; slide 5 ampersand versus and forms are excluded house-style variation.
Dash constructions: no third construction beyond the two operator-settled slide 12 items.
Speakability and terminology: all remaining audience-facing sentences and concept labels produced no reportable exception.

limitations: Source-closed audit using only the attached thesis, deck text extraction, deck PDF, request, schema, and audit brief.
Citation existence and years were accepted as operator-settled and were inventoried rather than independently re-derived.
Numbers, claim strength, causal language, layout, spelling, doubled words, and mathematical minus signs were outside this pass.
